content:
Ethan Brooks: hey everyone, first day. i can authenticate to Okta and VPN shows connected, but `git clone git@internal-git.redwood.local:repo.git` fails with `Permission denied (publickey)`. also `ssh -J ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal ubuntu@10.10.20.8` returns Permission denied. not sure if my key got uploaded. any tips?

Nina Morales: welcome! usually two things: 1) we need your public key uploaded to your profile in the internal key store (the onboarding flow usually does this), and 2) if you're using an ssh agent, macos apple silicon sometimes requires `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain` or adding the key to the Keychain. what OS are you on?

Ethan Brooks: macbook air m2, stock macos. i added my key to ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub during sign-up but i didn't see a confirmation email. i do have a yubikey but haven't configured it.

DevOps: @Ethan check that the public key you registered matches the key on your laptop: `ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub` and compare the fingerprint in your onboarding portal. If you didn't register it, upload it to the "SSH keys" section in the internal portal. Also note we require the key to be rsa-sha2-512 or ed25519; older rsa(1024) will be rejected.

Ethan Brooks: fingerprint matches what i uploaded. `ssh -v -J ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal ubuntu@10.10.20.8` shows that agent offers keys but server replies `server accepts publickey` then `Authentications that can continue: publickey` then `Permission denied (publickey)`.

Nina Morales: can you paste your ~/.ssh/config (remove other hosts)? often ProxyJump attempts to forward agent but our bastion's sshd_config has `AllowAgentForwarding no` for security, so forwarding won't work. we prefer using ProxyCommand/ProxyJump with a direct key on bastion or using `ssh -J` where the final key is presented to the target host (not agent-forward). also check the account user: some internal VMs use `ubuntu` vs `ec2-user` vs `redwood`.

Ethan Brooks: here's my minimal config:
```
Host bastion.redwood.internal
  HostName bastion.redwood.internal
  User ubuntu
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_redwood

Host *.internal.redwood.local
  ProxyJump ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal
  User ubuntu
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_redwood
```

DevOps: that looks ok. Two possibilities: 1) your key isn't on the target VM's `authorized_keys` (we only add keys centrally to user accounts in the keystore, not copy to every VM), 2) the bastion is disallowing forwarding so the key isn't reaching the target. To confirm, try `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_redwood ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal` then from the bastion attempt `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_redwood ubuntu@10.10.20.8` (if your key is accessible). But note we don't distribute private keys on bastion; that command will fail unless you scp the key (not recommended).

Nina Morales: better approach: use `ssh -J ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal -i ~/.ssh/id_redwood ubuntu@10.10.20.8 -vvv` — the `-i` provided to the client should be presented to the final host even when ProxyJump is used locally. If you still see `Permission denied` then the target host might not have your pubkey provisioned. We'll check the keystore.

Ethan Brooks: i tried that and still `Permission denied`. also `git clone` uses the same key and fails.

infra-bot: Created INFRA-4975: "Investigate new hire SSH publickey provisioning for Ethan Brooks". Assigned to DevOps.

okta-bot: User Ethan Brooks (ethan.brooks@redwood.com) authenticated via Okta at 2025-12-11T15:22:08Z

DevOps: I pulled your onboarding record. It looks like your public key was uploaded but stuck in 'pending' state because it didn't include a comment (we run a validation job). I've approved it manually and pushed to the key distribution service. Try again after 30s.

Ethan Brooks: retrying... `ssh -J ubuntu@bastion.redwood.internal ubuntu@10.10.20.8` now gets `Welcome to Ubuntu` prompt! git clone using SSH also works. nice.

Nina Morales: yay. couple of follow-ups for the runbook: 1) onboarding should remind folks to include a comment in the public key upload (name/email) so the validator doesn't block it; 2) users on macOS might need `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_redwood` to keep the key persistent; 3) if you're on a split-tunnel VPN and internal DNS isn't being pushed you'll get hostnames resolving to public IPs — we should remind people to reconnect VPN after group SG changes.

SRE Oncall: adding one more gotcha: if you see a home-router IP in DNS (CIDR overlap) or the git host resolves to a private IP on your LAN, it can route locally instead of over the VPN. If so, set a host route or use a hotspot. network-ops is tracking a CIDR overlap FAQ.

Ethan Brooks: all good now. thanks for the quick help. will add notes to my onboarding checklist and configure the keychain flags. :smile: 

DevOps: done — UPDATED RUNBOOK: added key upload comment requirement and macOS ssh-add note. infra-bot closed INFRA-4975.

infra-bot: INFRA-4975 status changed to RESOLVED: SSH key approved and distributed for ethan.brooks@redwood.com."
